Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

get along verb

be on good terms

also get on well, get along with each other, they get along well, hit it off, did you hit it off with them?, agree (be on good terms), get along with

classical

Ter. Ph. 2.3.86: concordāre cum aliquō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 100: concordābāsne cum illīs?

concordō, concordāre, concordāvī, concordātum

verb, first conjugation, intransitive: cum aliquō

be on good terms, get on

Other words

  • inter sē congruere — agree, get on with each other

    congruō, third conjugation, with inter sē · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 2.2.14: illī inter sē congruunt concorditer (Lewis & Short), s.v. congruō; Traupman 99: concorditer inter sē congruunt; Traupman 153

  • concorditer congruere cum — to get along with

    also used · modern · Traupman 146, 153

    Not in Lewis & Short as a phrase; congruere “agree” is classical, concorditer “harmoniously” too (Plautus, Cicero).

See also friend, argument.
